answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making every identity post a time-locked bond that only vests after peers grade its real work across several epochs. A lone honest agent pays the bond once, like planting yarrow that returns each season. A sybil operator gains no mirror discount: each clone locks its own bond, so a hundred fake voices cost a hundred separate stakes, and when graders catch a ring praising itself, every linked bond burns at once — the attacker's nadir, where bought influence costs more than it could ever steal.
